set.st: July 1939: the three young Belote boys dug up a drain tile holding $1,880 in $5/$10/$20 gold (1882-1902) on the farm about 4 mi W of Bronson (sec 5, Bronson Twp); days later Frank Belote kicked up an iron pipe with $1,120 in gold 12 ft away. A second tile, plugged with concrete at both ends, which the boys had used as a toy smokestack, was never found again. Owner Kregger ordered no more digging and evicted the Belotes. The original owner, who died in 1904, was said to have buried several lots of gold; a buried safe was dug up on the farm 25+ years before 1939, and the owner had plowed up a pipe of gold the year before the tile find. Pin is on the family estate strip in the N half of sec. 5 (1894 and 1915 atlases), not the spot itself.
set.pl: About 4 mi W of Bronson: sec. 5 T7S R8W, Bronson Twp (1894 Branch County atlas parcel; the Battle Creek Enquirer's "2 mi east" looks like an error). 1915 atlas: same family estate, house at N end of the strip by the township-line road.
set.t: Strong site: two caches 12 ft apart in the house yard; a third plugged tile is unaccounted for. The 1915 Branch atlas shows the family's 89-acre estate as a N-S strip across the N half of sec. 5, Bronson Twp, house at the N end by the township-line road; check that house yard on the 1938-40 aerial. Access: private farm: permission.
pinev: Parcel-level: the 1915 Branch County atlas (Bronson p.53) shows the same family's 89-acre estate as a N-S strip across the N half of sec. 5 T7S R8W, house mark at the N end by the township-line road; pin between house and strip (about 450 m). The 1894 atlas parcel matches the AP's "4 mi W".
